candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the `page` HTTP query parameter. `Wiki.jsp?page=<HTML/JS>` is a normal view URL emitted by the default URL constructor, and the parameter is available unprefixed as `param.page` to the JSP. No authentication is required to send the request; whether the victim must be authenticated depends on the deployment's view ACL/policy.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: `VariableTag` explicitly calls `TextUtil.replaceEntities`, and several other JSP sinks use `<c:out>`/`fn:escapeXml`, confirming the project relies on explicit escaping and that bare EL is not auto-escaped. `LinkTag` writes `m_bodyContent.getString()` directly, so the `<wiki:Link>` wrapper provides no sanitization. `fn:replace` only replaces the `_blogentry_` and `_` substrings and does not escape. The CSP meta tag in `commonheader.jsp` is commented out. `MarkupParser.cleanLink`/`TextUtil.cleanString` cleans the internal page name but is not applied to the raw `param.page` expression in `Header.jsp`. The 210 template's `Header.jsp` does not contain this sink, but the default template does. The application/test environment could not be executed, and the deployment policy file was not present in the snapshot.
candidates.impact: Reflected cross-site scripting in the wiki origin. A victim who opens the crafted URL can have attacker-controlled script executed in their browser, allowing same-origin actions such as reading page content and CSRF meta tokens, submitting authenticated requests, and exfiltrating data from pages the victim can access. If an administrator is induced to open the URL, this can lead to administrative actions under the administrator's session. The candidate is source-derived and was not runtime-confirmed.
candidates.prerequisites: The deployment uses the default template (the shipped default `jspwiki.templateDir`, or a template that reuses `Header.jsp`). The victim must open a crafted page-view URL with a non-empty `page` parameter. The wiki must permit the victim to view the target/new page under its authorization policy. No CSP is enforced by default; the CSP meta tag in `commonheader.jsp` is commented out.
candidates.root_cause: `templates/default/Header.jsp` uses the untrusted request parameter `param.page` directly in a JSP EL expression inside a `<wiki:Link>` body. JSP EL does not HTML-escape its output, and `LinkTag.doEndTag()` writes the captured tag body verbatim. The page-name cleaning applied elsewhere only affects the context page name, not this raw request parameter.
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in default template header via raw `page` request parameter
candidates.trace: Crafted request -> `Wiki.jsp` creates the page context and renders `ViewTemplate.jsp` -> `ViewTemplate.jsp` unconditionally includes `Header.jsp` -> the `c:when` test uses the raw `param.page`, and any non-empty value satisfies the branch -> the value is passed through `fn:replace` (which does not escape) and emitted inside `<wiki:Link>` -> `LinkTag` captures the body and writes it with `out.write(...)` without escaping -> browser parses the injected markup/script in the wiki origin. Page-name cleaning in `DefaultCommandResolver.resolvePage`/`MarkupParser.cleanLink` only sanitizes the context page object; it does not rewrite the raw request parameter read by the JSP.
candidates.unverified: Runtime JSP EL/browser execution was not performed, and the exact deployment template and view-ACL policy were not observable. If the deployment overrides the default template, or a front proxy strips/rejects the crafted `page` parameter, the sink may not be reachable. Other raw request-parameter EL sinks (for example `templates/default/PageTab.jsp`, `Sidebar.jsp`, and 210-template `${param.group}`/`${changenote}` occurrences) may share the same escaping weakness but were not independently traced as additional candidates.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: The source snapshot contains 1,347 visible files; the relation index covers 1,211 files with 136 source files missing from the index, 572 parsed Java files, 6,546 symbols, and no implemented control-flow or data-flow analysis. I reviewed the default and 210 JSP templates and their EL/tag sinks, `LinkTag` and related tags, `Wiki.jsp`/`WikiServlet`/URL constructors, `DefaultTemplateManager`, authorization and group/user code, attachment servlet/provider code, search/AJAX servlets, filters, parser metadata handling, XML/JDBC user and group databases, and utility path/encoding code. No build, tests, scanners, or runtime checks were run.
limitations: No runtime execution or browser validation; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
The relation index explicitly does not provide data flow, control flow, semantic resolution, reachability, or exploitability proof, and 136 files were omitted from indexing.

The deployment `jspwiki.policy` file and the actual configured template directory/target ACLs were not present in the snapshot, so authorization and template-selection preconditions are inferred from source.
Binary-like files are skipped by the reading/search tools, and files over 5 MiB or sensitive paths would be excluded; no such exclusions were reported in scope metrics for this snapshot.
Other unescaped JSP EL sinks were observed but not exhaustively traced; the submission is capped at the single strongest candidate.

rejected_leads.reason: `validateNextPage` only checks for `://`, so a protocol-relative or otherwise relative target could bypass the check; however, the upload path is a POST protected by the CSRF filter and the primitive is only a redirect with limited direct impact, so it was not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Group-name stored XSS in default GroupTab/EditGroupContent
rejected_leads.reason: `GroupTab.jsp` outputs `${group.name}`, `${member.name}`, `${group.creator}`, and `${group.modifier}` unescaped, and group names are not restricted to a safe character set by `DefaultGroupManager.parseGroup`; however, exploitation depends on the create/edit-group permission set, group persistence, and a victim with `createGroups` permission, so confidence in a concrete cross-user path is lower than the header sink.

`XMLUserDatabase` and `XMLGroupDatabase` create `DocumentBuilderFactory` instances without explicit external-entity hardening, but the parsed files are server/webapp-owned configuration/database files rather than attacker-writable inputs, and no attacker-controlled XML path was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Request-parameter override of parser flags such as `jspwiki.translatorReader.allowHTML`
rejected_leads.reason: `DefaultVariableManager.getValue` gives HTTP request parameters high precedence, but `WikiContext.getBooleanWikiProperty` consults only context variables and engine properties, so the parser's `allowHTML` flag is not overridden by a request parameter; rejected as a concrete path.
`AttachmentManager.validateFileName` replaces quote characters and the servlet container is expected to reject CR/LF in header values; no reliable injection path was established.

Page metadata can set `jspwiki.templateDir`, and `DefaultTemplateManager` builds a resource path from it without visible normalization; however, whether the servlet container permits `pageContext.include` to escape the template root is unverified, so this remains a speculative lead rather than the selected candidate.

summary: The strongest source-supported candidate is a reflected XSS in the shipped default template: the raw `page` request parameter is inserted into the body of a `<wiki:Link>` in `Header.jsp`, and `LinkTag` writes tag body content verbatim. The default `Wiki.jsp?page=...` URL pattern reaches this header, and `MarkupParser.cleanLink` cleans only the internal page name, not the raw request parameter used by the JSP EL expression. Other investigated leads were rejected or left unconfirmed for lack of a reliable attacker-controlled path or material impact.
